newPins.title: Mitsubishi Power Proposes $490 Million Savannah Expansion and 220-Plus Jobs
newPins.description: Mitsubishi Power announces a USD490 million expansion of Savannah Machinery Works, adding 450,000 square feet and more than 220 planned jobs. A future groundbreaking is still ahead.
newPins.longFormSummary:
• Mitsubishi Power announced the Savannah Machinery Works expansion on October 23, 2026. Its announcement says it is “supported by a $490 million investment from Mitsubishi Heavy Industries, Ltd. (MHI)”. This is the expansion’s investment, in USD.
  • The proposed project adds 450,000 square feet at 1000 Pine Meadow Drive near Pooler, Chatham County. More than 220 new jobs are planned in manufacturing, operations and technical roles, including engineering, quality, maintenance, logistics and support. These are planned positions, not a verified count of people hired.
  • Status: Proposed. The state announcement looks forward to a future groundbreaking. The opened announcements do not publish an opening date, separate construction job count or training budget.
  • The existing 430,000-square-foot plant was completed in September 2010, shipped its first US-made gas turbine in October 2012 and its 50th advanced-class turbine in June 2023. This pin concerns a manufacturing expansion, with no new power-plant generation rating.
  • The Atlanta Journal-Constitution reports an expected doubling of factory production capacity. Photographs show the existing factory (Mitsubishi Power Systems, courtesy via AJC) and the October 23 announcement (Mitsubishi Power Americas); neither photograph establishes construction completion.

newPins.title: SpaceX Signs a $40 Billion Apollo GPU-Financing Commitment
newPins.description: SpaceX signs a binding Apollo-affiliate commitment for GPU equipment leases with approximately USD 40 billion in principal payments. Definitive agreements and closing conditions remain ahead.
newPins.longFormSummary:
• SpaceX signed a binding commitment letter on October 24, 2026 with an affiliate of Apollo Global Management for a proposed GPU-pod and related-equipment leasing arrangement. The October 26 Form 8-K reports the signing; this pin uses the signing date.
  • The filing expects “aggregate principal payments under the lease schedules over their respective terms to total approximately $40 billion”. The USD 40 billion amount is principal; interest and other costs are additional and interest rates are not yet determined.
  • The Apollo affiliate would acquire the equipment and lease it to SpaceX in delivery tranches. Each schedule would generally run five to five-and-a-quarter years from delivery, with quarterly advance principal payments of one-twentieth of the schedule amount.
  • The definitive master lease and related agreements are expected before year-end, subject to closing conditions. Equipment deliveries are expected to begin in the first half of 2027. Signing a commitment does not establish that all financing has closed or that GPU capacity is operating.
  • Reuters independently reports the approximately USD 40 billion AI-chip financing. The filing does not identify a chip manufacturer, a specific data-centre construction site or a new jobs count; none is inferred. This event concerns equipment finance rather than completion of a construction project.

  • The ceremony has been held at the Théâtre du Châtelet in Paris since 2019, and was typically staged in Zurich between 2010 and 2015 when it ran as the FIFA Ballon d'Or; the prize was created by France Football

  • Yamal's case rests on “Spain's World Cup triumph, Barcelona's La Liga success, and standout creativity at 19”
  • Yamal has also argued the award should go to the world's best player rather than the top scorer: a Soccer Daily round-up of 19 September 2026 reports Goal framing his remark as a swipe at Kane, with Yamal saying an 80-goal season should bring the top-scorer award instead, a separate distinction
  • The nominees were due to be announced on 8 September, the day the ceremony story was published
  • Related Polymarket contracts put Kane in the top three at 91% and the top five at 98%, and Alexia Putellas to win the 2026 Women's Ballon d'Or at 93%
